content: SMG1, also known as serine/threonine-protein kinase SMG1, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the SMG1 gene. This enzyme is a member of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-related kinase (PIKK) protein family. The SMG1 gene encodes a protein that plays a critical role in the process of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), which is a key component of the mRNA surveillance complex. This protein exhibits kinase activity and is believed to contribute to NMD by phosphorylating the UPF1 protein, also known as the regulator of nonsense transcripts 1. This phosphorylation is essential for the proper functioning of the NMD pathway. Additionally, alternative splicing of SMG1 transcripts has been observed, but the complete structures of these variants have not yet been fully characterized. SMG1 has been demonstrated to interact with other proteins, including PRKCI (Protein Kinase C, iota) and UPF1, suggesting its involvement in complex regulatory networks within the cell.
